wiki_text: On October 10, 2025, Tokyo Gas, Kyuden International, and Truong Thanh Viet Nam Group broke ground on the Thai Binh LNG-to-power project in Thai Thuy district. The US$2 billion project, developed through Thai Binh LNG Power JSC, comprises an LNG receiving terminal and a 1,500 MW combined-cycle power plant, with commercial operation targeted by 2029 and a power purchase agreement with EVN expected to be finalized in 2026.

On March 2, 2026, Japan Petroleum Exploration Co. (JAPEX) announced it would exit the LNG terminal project at Nam Dinh Vu Industrial Park in Hai Phong City, transferring all of its shares in developer ITECO JSC to ITECO's business partners after feasibility studies begun in January 2022 found the project's economic challenges difficult to overcome. The planned first phase comprised a 50,000 m3 LNG storage tank and berthing facilities handling up to 650,000 tonnes per year.

In July 2025, authorities of the Nghi Son Economic Zone cancelled the tender to select an investor for the US$2.4 billion Nghi Son LNG power plant and import terminal for the third time after no bids were submitted by the June 10, 2025 deadline. Earlier shortlisted bidders had included a SOVICO-JERA consortium, PetroVietnam Power-T&T Group, a KEPCO-KOGAS-Daewoo E&C-Anh Phat consortium, Gulf Energy Development, and SK. In September 2025 a JERA delegation expressed renewed interest in implementing the project at a meeting with the Thanh Hoa People's Committee.

Vingroup and VinEnergo broke ground on the Hai Phong LNG power plant project on September 26, 2025, within the Tan Trao industrial park. The associated LNG import infrastructure is planned at the mouth of the Van Uc River, where water depth of -16 m would accommodate LNG carriers of 180,000 m3 or more, with one berth, one FSRU, and a pipeline to the 4,800 MW (2x phases) power plant, which is targeted to be operational by the end of 2030.
